subject: biology
title: Studying the brain and treating nervous system damage
key_idea: Scientists study the brain using patients with damage, electrical stimulation and scans such as CT and PET. The skull and the brain's complexity make it hard to study. Brain and spinal damage is hard to treat because nerves do not repair. (Separate science)

blocks.text: (Separate science) The brain sits inside the skull, so scientists cannot just look at it working. This section covers the methods used and why each has limits.

items: **Studying patients** with brain damage, for example after an accident. Scientists link the damaged area to the problem the person has.
**Electrical stimulation**: stimulating a small part of the brain and observing what the person does or feels.
**CT and MRI scans**: show the structure of the brain without opening the skull.
**PET scans**: show which parts of the brain are active, so they can be linked to a function.
**Animal experiments**: part of an animal's brain is damaged, or removed, and the animal is observed.
The brain is protected by the skull, so it is difficult to reach.
The brain is very complex. It has a very large number of neurones with many connections, and several areas may be involved in one function.
Results from animals may be different to humans.
There are **ethical issues**, such as harming or killing animals for experiments.
It can be hard to find patients who are willing to take part, and testing could cause harm.
Case studies are hard to interpret. A single patient may not show a reliable pattern.
Scans let scientists see inside the skull without surgery.
PET and similar scans link a brain region to a function.
Complexity, access and ethics all limit what we can learn.

sections.heading: Why brain and spinal damage is hard to treat

blocks.text: (Separate science) Damage to the brain or spinal cord is often permanent. Diseases of the brain are also hard to treat.

items: The skull protects the brain, so it is difficult to access a tumour.
Nerves in the brain and spinal cord do not repair or regenerate, so damage is often irreversible.
Surgery risks damaging healthy parts of the brain. Treatments can have side effects.
After spinal damage, impulses cannot pass the injury, so signals do not reach the rest of the body.
A trial with a small number of patients may not show the treatment works for everyone.
A short trial cannot show whether an improvement lasts.
A new cell count in a scan does not prove that symptoms have improved.
Risks and possible damage must be assessed before a treatment is offered to all patients.

checks.q: Give two reasons why it is difficult to treat a brain tumour.
checks.a: Any two from: the brain is protected by the skull so it is difficult to access; nerves do not repair or regenerate; the risk of damage to healthy parts of the brain.

checks.q: Give one ethical issue with studying the brain using animals.
checks.a: Damaging, harming or killing live animals for experiments.

checks.q: State one way a scan helps scientists investigate brain function.
checks.a: It lets them see which part of the brain is active without opening the skull.

mistakes.wrong: A traditional MRI scanner can be used for anyone.
mistakes.right: A traditional MRI scanner cannot be used if people cannot stay still. A functional MRI (fMRI) scanner allows the person to move.

mistakes.wrong: An fMRI scan only shows what the brain looks like.
mistakes.right: It shows which part of the brain is active or inactive, so the person can be asked to do a task while it is scanned.

worked_example.question:
In most MRI scanners the person being scanned needs to stay completely still. A functional MRI (fMRI) scanner allows a person to move while the scanner makes images of the person's brain activity.

Suggest how the fMRI scanner could help to find out more about the brain damage a person has.
answer_points: The person can be asked to do different tasks while the scan is taken.
This shows which part of the brain is active or inactive.
It can be compared with a person without brain damage, to see exactly where the damage is.
worked_example.tip: Any three points score. The scanner is also useful for people who cannot stay still.

mistakes.wrong: Another way a brain tumour can be detected is an eye test.
mistakes.right: If the question already gives eye tests, give another method: CT or PET scanning. MRI or X-ray is also accepted.

mistakes.wrong: A brain tumour is easy to treat because damaged nerves repair themselves.
mistakes.right: Nerves do not repair or regenerate. A brain tumour is difficult to treat because of this, the skull, and the risk of damaging the brain.

worked_example.question:
Eye tests can detect some brain tumours.

Describe why a brain tumour is difficult to treat.
answer_points: The brain is protected by the skull (bone), so it is difficult to access.
Nerves do not repair or regenerate, and there is a risk of damage to the brain (healthy cells).
worked_example.tip: A description including two points scores both marks. Any two from the four points are enough.

mistakes.wrong: It is unethical to study the brain.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Name the issue, such as experimenting on or harming live animals.
This is ignored. Say it is difficult to get research subjects who are willing to participate or give consent.

mistakes.wrong: The treatment may have long term effects.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Say the treatment may have side effects, or that it must be shown to be safe and effective in the long term.

worked_example.question:
Parkinson's disease results in a reduction in dopamine in neurones deep in the brain. To try to identify the cause of the disease, scientists use two methods:
• animals have part of their brain deliberately damaged and are then observed
• the brains of people with the disease are studied.

Explain any difficulties scientists may encounter when using these two methods for studying Parkinson's disease.
answer_points: There are ethical issues with experimenting on live animals.
Results in animals may be different to humans.
The brain is very complex, with many different connections, and some areas are difficult to reach.
It is difficult to get research subjects willing to take part, and it could cause further harm to people with the disease.
worked_example.tip: Any four points score one mark each.
